C-R6-PREFERENCE-CONTROLS-324.Summary: Make adaptive defaults subordinate to saved, explicit and domain-derived values, and give each account direct control over learning, reset and safe pinned defaults.
C-R6-PREFERENCE-CONTROLS-324.Problem: The current preference layer ignores synthetic events when recording choices but does not preserve value origin. A late MutationObserver or async helper can therefore reapply a learned default after a saved view or a manual choice. Users also cannot disable learning, clear learned frequency or explicitly pin a safe default without affecting work data.

Goals.Goal: Introduce one UI value-origin contract with precedence saved/explicit > domain-derived > pinned/learned suggestion > static fallback.
Prevent delayed suggestion application from overwriting a saved view, a trusted user edit or deterministic domain-derived value.
Store account-scoped learning enabled and pinned safe-default controls using the existing preference table without a migration.
Allow resetting only learned frequency for the current account while preserving work data, explicit settings, pins and other accounts.
Make pinned safe defaults outrank frequency and continue deterministic domain-derived behavior when learning is disabled.

Constraints.Constraint: No SQLite migration, no work-domain mutation and no VERSION change.
Programmatic substitutions and synthetic events never increment frequency.
Only an explicit safe allowlist can be pinned; status/ACL/execution/destructive decisions remain never-learn.
Account controls are isolated by existing account_scope and participate in ordinary backup/restore.
Disabling learning suppresses frequency reads/writes but does not disable deterministic domain-derived defaults or explicit pinned values.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Introduce an ML recommendation engine or change UI geometry by statistics.
Reset saved plan/fact views, calendar start settings, work objects, evidence or audit.
Pin people assignments, ACL roles, completion/cancel states, delete/archive actions or free text.
Add a new table or migration for settings that fit the existing auxiliary preference projection.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A saved plan/fact view remains authoritative after preference reapplication and DOM mutation.
A trusted manual input made before a delayed preference response is never overwritten by that response.
Domain-derived values remain stronger than pinned or learned defaults.
Per-account controls can disable/enable learning, reset learned frequency and pin/unpin safe defaults; another account is unchanged.
Pinned safe default wins over a more frequent learned value.
With learning disabled, new frequency choices are not written and learned rankings are not applied, while deterministic domain-derived behavior still runs.
Existing never-learn status protection remains and control rows never appear as normal preference contexts.
Desktop/mobile preference controls are compact, Russian, keyboard usable, no modal cascade and no motion dependency; prefers-reduced-motion remains unchanged.
Targeted controls/origin/browser regressions and ordinary project CI pass on one exact PR head.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Exact-head evidence proves account isolation, reset boundaries, pin-over-frequency, saved/explicit/domain origin precedence and disabled-learning behavior without schema changes.
